description: Seed knowledge set for the Bosch example machine (#89). Read by the import (#90). Elements are referenced by the assembly group identifier (CAD definition name), which stays the same across imports; the import resolves it to the record id.

properties.name: Purpose of the station
properties.statement: The station takes 3D-printed parts, clamps them automatically on the robot, removes the support structures by chiselling and returns the part to the operator.
properties.reasoning: Based on a prior process-pipeline study and in-house post-processing experience.

properties.name: Process sequence
properties.statement: The operator requests the drawer and places the part in a fixture. The gripper picks it at 3 pins spaced 120 degrees apart, the robot runs the chisel (or dry-ice) process, then puts the part back in the drawer.

properties.name: Single-part operation
properties.statement: The cell handles one part at a time, not a double system.
properties.condition: If the cycle time requires it.
properties.recommendation: Add a buffer or a double drawer. Alternative: the robot comes to an opened door and the operator clips the part in.

properties.name: Referencing the part before chiselling
properties.statement: Each part gets one attempt: if it sits 1 cm off, the chisel destroys it.
properties.recommendation: Derive reference points from the CAD and the 3-point fixture and check them with a touch probe before chiselling. Alternatives are a laser profile scanner or a camera; the camera is costly and suits high volumes.

properties.name: Welded steel base frame
properties.statement: The base frame is welded from 160 x 160 mm square hollow sections with a 6 mm wall.
properties.reasoning: Chosen for the robot dynamics. It also seals better against dust underneath than a light frame.

properties.name: Base plate weight
properties.statement: The dimensions are a first sketch. With a 30 mm base plate over the whole area the frame weighs about 2.5 t.
properties.recommendation: Use a solid plate only under the robot and sheet metal elsewhere.

properties.name: Width under truck limit
properties.statement: The frame is about 2.45 m wide. Length can vary.
properties.reasoning: Stays under the 2.50 m truck width that needs no special transport permit.

properties.name: Control cabinet size
properties.statement: Standard cabinet, 2 x 800 mm wide and 600 mm deep. It holds PLC, safety and robot control, with a water cooling unit on top.
properties.reasoning: 600 mm depth so the robot controller fits.

properties.name: Cabinet copied from Station 75
properties.statement: The cabinet was copied from Station 75, which was twice the size, and cut down as a placeholder.

properties.name: Cabinet on the base plate
properties.statement: The cabinet is mounted on the base plate.
properties.reasoning: The cell ships as one unit with nothing to reconnect.

properties.name: Chisel on a Schunk column system
properties.statement: The chisel assembly is mounted on a Schunk column system. Height and lateral offset are adjustable, and a second tool can be clamped on.

properties.name: Hopper into a KLT drawer
properties.statement: Removed supports fall through a hopper into a standard KLT bin in a drawer.
properties.reasoning: Concept taken from a Bamberg station for breaking off sprues.

properties.name: Hopper not sealed
properties.statement: The hopper connects the cell interior to the outside. Sealing, for example with a door, is not designed yet.
properties.consequence: Dust and particles can leave the cell.

properties.name: Pneumatic chisel too weak
properties.statement: The pneumatic tool seen at Fraunhofer is made for fine filing work in tool and mould making (about 130 l/min of air, variants at 9,000 and 3,000 strokes per minute). It pushed the supports off instead of chiselling them.
properties.recommendation: Check the impact energy (FEM) and ask Fraunhofer why they chose it. Prefer an electric tool for an all-electric cell.

properties.name: HMI from the SFP test bench
properties.statement: Standard Beckhoff screen with a function bar on a cantilever arm, taken from the SFP test bench. A standard status light sits on top.

properties.name: Calculated robot paths
properties.statement: Paths are calculated for each part, not taught, so a calculation error could drive the robot into the guarding.
properties.recommendation: Keep fixed moves (pick and place) as separate programs and reject generated points outside an allowed window with an error message.

properties.name: Limit the robot workspace
properties.statement: Use KUKA safety technology to limit the workspace of a large robot. It costs extra validation and a reference run about once per shift.
properties.reasoning: The customer's site layout is unknown.
properties.condition: A recommendation from the accident-insurance body (BG) might allow skipping it if no workstation is nearby. Decide in the project phase.
